newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki off but Aamulehti soars on MTV merger.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki off but Aamulehti soars on MTV merger.

text.p: Shares fell on Tuesday in sluggish trade amid continued international uncertainty, but media group Aamulehti soared after announcing a merger with home commercial television channel MTV Oy, brokers said.

The HEX index fell 0.39 percent to 2,826.46 points and the FOX portfolio and derivatives benchmark fell 0.77 percent to 983.83. Unusally active trade in Aamulehti accounted for seven percent of thin 339 million markka overall volume.
Aamulehti surged 35.50 markka or 23 percent to 190.00.
"The new company looks extremely attractive ... I have a feeling we haven't seen the ceiling yet," one broker said.

Aamulehti and MTV said they plan to merge into a new company, of which Aamulehti's current owners would get some 60 percent, mainly to meet the challenges of digitalisation which are wiping out distinctions between different media.
Telecoms major Nokia, which will be a leading owner in the new media group, fell 3.00 markka to 300.00 despite the news.
"It's been quite subdued lately, and I don't expect overall sentiment to change for a while," one broker said. "The caution is still clearly perceptible."
Coming Q1 reports, especially on Friday from Nokia's rival Ericsson, may boost trading interest, he added.
Confectionery and packaging group Huhtamaki also bucked the trend in lively trade, adding 1.00 markka to 233.50.
But forestries were not helped by word from Metsa-Botnia that it would raise its long-fibre pulp prices to $580 from $520 at the start of May; the sector sub-index fell 1.21 percent.
"Forestry shares have been rising quite fast recently, now that the market was generally depressed they recoiled a bit," one broker said, adding the trend was similar in the U.S.
"Pulp price hikes are largely discounted in prices already," said another, but added that markets were watching closely if the hikes would hold.
